question.text: Mr. Karthik Balaji's Cat I SSF 'Chola Resolution Fund' is underwriting 'distressed debt' in a going-concern textile company. Per Chapter 9, distressed debt financing is BEST described as:

answer.text: Providing equity capital only, never debt.
A pure equity buyout of a liquidated company post-bankruptcy.

Debt refinancing that helps clear accumulated dues, reduce leverage, and provide relief — targeting companies at high risk of bankruptcy or restructuring but still going concerns; usually senior loans with adequate collateral at higher cost than performing companies.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'Distressed debt opportunities … typically deal with financing companies stretched for cash … The distress capital financing is essentially a debt refinancing that will help to clear up the accumulated dues, reduce leverage and provide relief to the company from either a restructuring or a bankruptcy. Usually such financing are provided as senior loans with adequate collaterals and at a higher cost than what a performing company may get.' The Trap: Option A contradicts 'debt refinancing'. Option C confuses distressed-debt with liquidation buyouts. Option B describes Cat III strategies (excluded). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covered distressed-debt strategy. III-A/C covers IBC framework. XIX-B covers Cat III arbitrage (comparison only — NOT Cat I/II). Manager's Pro-Tip: In distressed-debt deals, insist on a cash-sweep plus an EBITDA covenant. Distressed borrowers often have volatile cash flows; a DSCR trigger and a working-capital floor protect the AIF from a second-round default.
